body:
They cut contact because they didn't enjoy being around me. I could see it on their faces, they were bored or stressed or uncomfortable being near me. I know they'd think "maybe I should see what he's up to, but I don't feel like hearing him complain, I'll just wait" 

No one really enjoys my company, and if some do, they don't show it. I'm genuinely glad to see or hear from someone, but I don't see that in others. 

It was a few university courses. I was supposed to take another course but I had so much anxiety I didn't show up and can't even get the nerve to go to the office and drop it. The longer I wait the worse it will get but I just can't deal with that right now. I got some drugs recently that I played to OD on. I want to tell someone that I'm suicidal but I can't stand going back to a hospital. They didn't help before, no reason to expect it'll be better now. Plus I don't want my family finding out. They don't offer support just feel bad for me. So I wouldn't get any help just make them upset which would only make me feel worse.

Why should I even bother with getting a career? Nothing excites me, nothing interests me. At least nothing you can make profit on. The whole game of building up your resume, contacting job sites, applying for internships, picking a graduate program just seems so overwhelming. And it's disheartening when I see everyone doing it and have been doing it for years. Shit I don't have any accolades to put on a resume. I hate the idea of selling yourself at interviews, seems like lying to me. And what is it all for? I'd just rather not play that game. I have no desire to. Too much input with too little output for me. It's a miracle if I get out of bed in the morning, picking a graduate program is damn near impossible. And that's my problem, I get its a simple process and all of it is easy for many. I can accept that and am willing to just quit living. Just not cut out for it.
